indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.2.2.1 Demonstrate understanding of the life cycle of a plant
indicator.objective: Observe the life cycle of a plant (okra or maize plant)

skills.description: Identify the seed as the starting stage of the plant life cycle.
Describe germination as the sprouting of a seed into a seedling.
Describe the growth stage (seedling becomes a mature plant with leaves, stem, roots).
Identify flowering as a stage in the life cycle (okra/maize produce flowers).
Recognise that fruits/seeds are produced, completing the cycle.
Arrange the stages of the life cycle in the correct order.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: A seed is not part of the life cycle.
Plants do not produce seeds until they are old.
Germination and growth are the same stage.
Maize plants do not produce flowers.
The life cycle stops at the mature plant.
Fruits are not connected to seeds.

questions.stem: What is the first stage of a plant's life cycle?
hints: It is small and can be planted.
It grows into a new plant.
questions.explanation: The seed is the first stage of the plant life cycle.
questions.misconception: A seed is not part of the life cycle.

questions.stem: Where does a new plant come from?
hints: It is planted in the soil.
questions.explanation: A new plant grows from a seed.
questions.misconception: Plants grow from stones.

questions.stem: What is the first stage of a plant's life cycle?
hints: It is planted in the soil.
questions.explanation: The seed is the first stage of the plant life cycle.
questions.misconception: The life cycle starts with a flower.

questions.stem: What is germination?
options: The sprouting of a seed into a seedling
hints: It is when a seed starts to grow.
questions.explanation: Germination is the sprouting of a seed into a seedling.
questions.misconception: Germination is the same as growth.

questions.stem: What do we call the young plant that comes out of a germinating seed?
hints: It has just started to grow.
questions.explanation: The young plant that comes out of a germinating seed is called a seedling.
questions.misconception: A seedling is a mature plant.

questions.stem: Describe what happens during germination.
answer: a seed sprouts and a small seedling appears
the seed begins to grow into a seedling
a shoot comes out of the seed
hints: Think about a seed starting to grow.
questions.explanation: During germination, a seed sprouts and a small seedling appears.
questions.misconception: Germination is when the plant flowers.

questions.stem: What happens during the growth stage of a plant?
options: The seedling becomes a mature plant with more leaves
hints: It develops more leaves and a stronger stem.
questions.explanation: During the growth stage, the seedling grows into a mature plant with more leaves, a taller stem and deeper roots.
questions.misconception: Growth happens after flowering.

questions.stem: Which of these shows that a plant is in the growth stage?
options: It is getting taller and developing more leaves
questions.explanation: A plant in the growth stage gets taller and develops more leaves.
questions.misconception: Growth is the same as flowering.

questions.stem: What happens to a seedling during the growth stage?
answer: it grows into a mature plant with more leaves and a taller stem
it gets bigger and develops more leaves
hints: More leaves and a stronger stem.
questions.explanation: During the growth stage, the seedling grows into a mature plant with more leaves and a taller stem.
questions.misconception: The seedling stays the same size.

questions.stem: A pupil observes a maize plant that is taller than the seedling stage but has not yet produced flowers. What stage is the plant in?
hints: It has grown but not flowered yet.
questions.explanation: The plant is in the growth stage because it has grown taller but has not yet produced flowers.
questions.misconception: The plant is in the flowering stage.

questions.stem: What happens during the flowering stage of a maize plant?
hints: Maize plants produce tassels and silks.
questions.explanation: During the flowering stage, the maize plant produces flowers (tassels and silks).
questions.misconception: Maize plants do not produce flowers.

questions.stem: Why is the flowering stage important in the life cycle of a plant?
answer: flowers help the plant produce fruits and seeds
questions.explanation: The flowering stage is important because flowers help the plant produce fruits and seeds for the next generation.
questions.misconception: Flowers are not important.

questions.stem: A farmer notices that his okra plants have started producing yellow flowers. What stage of the life cycle are the plants in?
questions.explanation: The okra plants are in the flowering stage because they have started producing flowers.
questions.misconception: The plants are still in the growth stage only.

questions.stem: What happens after the flowering stage in the life cycle of a plant?
questions.explanation: After flowering, the plant produces fruits and seeds, completing the life cycle.
questions.misconception: The life cycle stops at flowering.

questions.stem: What is the final stage of the life cycle of a maize plant?
questions.explanation: The final stage is the production of fruits (cobs) and seeds, which can grow into new plants.
questions.misconception: The life cycle ends at flowering.

questions.stem: What does a plant produce at the end of its life cycle?
hints: These can grow into new plants.
questions.explanation: At the end of its life cycle, a plant produces fruits and seeds.
questions.misconception: Plants do not produce seeds.

questions.stem: A maize cob is full of maize seeds. What does this show about the plant's life cycle?
options: The plant has completed its life cycle by producing seeds
The plant is still in the germination stage
The plant has not yet flowered
hints: The cycle is complete when seeds are formed.
questions.explanation: The cob full of seeds shows that the plant has completed its life cycle by producing seeds for the next generation.
questions.misconception: Seeds are not part of the life cycle.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly shows the life cycle of a maize plant?
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is: seed → germination → growth → flowering → fruiting/seeds.
questions.misconception: Flowering comes before growth.

questions.stem: Arrange these stages in the correct order: flowering, seed, growth, germination, fruiting.
questions.explanation: The correct order is: seed, germination, growth, flowering, fruiting.
questions.misconception: Flowering comes before growth.

questions.stem: In groups, plant a maize or okra seed and observe it over several weeks. Record the stages you observe (germination, growth, flowering, fruiting). Present your findings to the class.

criteria.description: Planted a seed and cared for it
Observed and recorded at least three stages of the life cycle
Arranged the stages in the correct order
Presented findings clearly to the class

hints: Plant the seed and water it.
Watch for germination, growth, flowers, and fruits.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The life cycle stops at the mature plant.
